title: Pluginize benchmark harness: dataset fixtures, sampled prompting, and lightweight eval adapters
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need to refactor the existing benchmark harness to support a plugin model for datasets, prompt sampling strategies, and lightweight eval adapters used during profile generation. Current harness code paths conflate dataset loading, prompt templating, and runner orchestration which leads to duplicated logic across onboarding flows and brittle ad-hoc integrations for new model types. This ticket delivers a minimal plugin API, a small registry, and a migration path for two sample adapters (classification accuracy runner and contextual generation runner) so we can reliably produce performance profiles across model variants and quantization levels.

Goals:
- Define a tiny, stable plugin interface for: dataset fixtures, prompt samplers (stratified / edge-case focused), and eval runners.
- Implement a registry + discovery mechanism so new plugins can be registered at runtime and referenced in onboarding manifests.
- Provide two canonical adapters: (1) classification_accuracy_adapter (batchable, uses top-k metrics), (2) contextual_continuation_adapter (generation-oriented, measures latency-per-token and PPL-style metrics).
- Add sampling utilities to produce deterministic prompt subsets (seeded, stratified by length / label) used in profile generation.
- Ensure generated profiles include sampler metadata, dataset provenance, and runner version to make profiles reproducible.

Non-goals:
- Do not change core runtime serving behavior. This is a harness-level change only.
- Not introducing heavy orchestration (no distributed job runner in this ticket).

Technical approach:
1) Plugin API: A single-file interface definition with three plugin types: DatasetPlugin, SamplerPlugin, RunnerPlugin. Each plugin exposes a minimal set of callables: load_manifest() -> dict (dataset metadata), iter_examples(seed:int) -> iterator[str|dict], run_batch(batch: list) -> list[dict]. Implementations must be pure-Python and side-effect free during iteration to preserve determinism.
2) Registry: A small YAML-based registry file (tests/plugins/registry.yaml) and a runtime registry that can be extended via environment variable (BENCH_HARNESS_PLUGINS_PATH). Registry entries include id, version, path, and capabilities.
3) Sampling utils: Implement stratified_sampler(length_buckets=[0-64,65-256,256+], per_bucket_n=100, seed=...) and edge_case_sampler(label_ratios={rare:0.05}). Sampler outputs are stable and recorded in profile metadata.
4) Runner adapters: Implement two runner adapters with CI smoke tests and a local perf harness: classification_accuracy_adapter (vectorized scoring, uses cached embeddings optionally) and contextual_continuation_adapter (supports streaming simulation and per-token latency measurement hooks).
5) Migration: Provide shims for existing harness entrypoints so current onboarding manifests still run. Add a CLI flag --plugin-mode and a config toggle in onboarding manifests to reference plugin ids. Gradual rollout: default to legacy mode until all onboarding flows are validated.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests covering plugin API surface (>=90% coverage for new modules).
- Integration test that registers the two adapters and runs a full profile generation for a small public dataset (e.g., glue_sample_small) under CI, producing a profile JSON with sampler metadata.
- Documentation: Confluence page + README for plugin authors and a template plugin in examples/plugins/.
- Backward compatibility: existing onboarding manifests run unchanged unless --plugin-mode is specified.
- Performance: benchmark harness end-to-end runtime overhead when using pluginized path must be <= 5% compared to legacy harness for sample runs.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: API design + registry schema proposal + small prototype for samplers.
- Week 2: Implement runner adapters + unit tests.
- Week 3: Migration shims + CI integration test + docs.
- Week 4: Validation with two onboarding teams, gather feedback, iterate.

Telemetry and observability:
- Add profiler logs to profile JSON: plugin_ids, plugin_versions, sampler_seed, sample_counts, total_examples, runner_time_ms, per_token_stats.
- Emit harness-level metrics to metrics pipeline: bench.harness.run.started, bench.harness.run.finished, bench.runner.latency.p50/p95.
